name: The Bridges
lesson: Following lateral movement: admin-share writes and remote service creation, RDP chains that break the allowed paths, and coordinated containment.
pivot_tip: Pivot on src_ip for RDP. t.brooks RDPs from IT-ADM-03 every day. From a file server, never.
reaction: A new RDP session just opened from JUMP-02 to BACKUP-01. VELVET LOCUST is spreading its bets.

e601.title: 5145: ADMIN$ write on FS-CORE-01
e601.tip: Copy a binary into ADMIN$, then create a service that runs it: the classic remote-execution pattern, PsExec style.

e602.title: 7045: service installed on FS-CORE-01
lines: Event 7045  A service was installed in the system
Start Type   : demand start      Account: LocalSystem
Installed by : t.brooks via remote Service Control Manager (from 10.20.4.142)
No change ticket. 'Halcyon Telemetry' is not a product Halcyon IT owns.
e602.tip: Services named after the company are a favorite disguise. Check against your software inventory.

e603.title: RDP sessions on JUMP-02 and VAULT-DB-01
lines: Session clipboard: enabled   Drive redirection: enabled
e603.tip: Follow the source addresses hop by hop: finance desk, file server, jump server, vault.

e604.title: Approved admin paths (NET-POLICY)
lines: RDP to JUMP-02          : only from IT-ADM-* (10.20.2.0/24)
RDP to tier-0 servers   : only from JUMP-02, MFA required (MFA rollout: 40%)
SMB ADMIN$ on servers   : only from IT-ADM-* and SCCM
Exception in place: VAULT-DB-01 MFA pending (payroll vendor dependency)
e604.tip: Knowing the allowed paths turns lateral movement into a simple question: which hops break policy?

e605.title: 7045: same service on BACKUP-01
lines: Event 7045  A service was installed in the system
Installed by : t.brooks via remote SCM (from 10.20.2.20, JUMP-02)
BACKUP-01 holds the only online copy of last night's backups.
e605.tip: Adversaries who plan ransomware go after backups first. This is a warning sign for later.

objectives.title: Check the file server
objectives.desc: Investigate FS-CORE-01 for the admin-share write.
hints: The Core File Server node.
Press E at FS-CORE-01.
Open '5145: ADMIN$ write on FS-CORE-01'.

objectives.title: Every ADMIN$ write
objectives.desc: Hunt the share table for access to the hidden ADMIN$ share.
objectives.success: Two hops: FS-CORE-01 from the finance desk, BACKUP-01 from the jump server.
hints: The share field holds names like \\*\ADMIN$.
Use ~ to match part of the share name.
search share where share~"ADMIN$"

objectives.title: What did they install?
objectives.desc: Find services whose image is the dropped binary, svchelper.exe.
objectives.success: The same fake service on two servers. Remote service execution.
hints: The 5145 event named the file that was written.
Search the image field for it.
search svc where image~"svchelper"

objectives.title: The first bridge
objectives.desc: Find t.brooks network logons coming from Mira's workstation (10.20.4.142).
objectives.solution: search auth where account="t.brooks" and src_ip="10.20.4.142"
objectives.success: NTLM network logon to FS-CORE-01 from the finance desk, 2 seconds before the ADMIN$ write.
hints: Two conditions: the account and the source address.
account="t.brooks" and src_ip="10.20.4.142".
search auth where account="t.brooks" and src_ip="10.20.4.142"

objectives.title: Follow the hops
objectives.desc: Collect the service install, the RDP sessions, the approved paths, and BACKUP-01's record.
hints: FS-CORE-01 has a second item, plus JUMP-02, NET-POLICY, and BACKUP-01.
Press E at each.
Open all four records.

objectives.title: RDP that breaks policy
objectives.desc: Find RDP logons (logon_type 10) that did NOT come from IT-ADM-03 (10.20.2.33).
objectives.solution: search auth where logon_type=10 and src_ip!="10.20.2.33"
objectives.success: FS-CORE-01 to JUMP-02, then JUMP-02 to VAULT-DB-01. They're at the vault door.
hints: RDP shows up as logon_type 10. Tom's normal RDP comes from 10.20.2.33.
Combine logon_type=10 with src_ip != the admin desk.
search auth where logon_type=10 and src_ip!="10.20.2.33"

objectives.title: Draw the bridges
objectives.desc: Press L. Order the lateral movement.

events.label: NTLM network logon as t.brooks: WS-FIN-0142 -> FS-CORE-01
'Halcyon Telemetry Helper' service runs svchelper.exe on FS-CORE-01
svchelper.exe pushed to BACKUP-01 via ADMIN$ from JUMP-02

objectives.success: Desk, file server, jump server, vault, and backups. The map of the intrusion is complete.
hints: Check the timestamps: 10:04, 10:12, 10:19, 10:26.
The logon comes before the file write; the service comes after it.
Logon, ADMIN$ write, service, RDP to JUMP-02, RDP to the vault, BACKUP-01.

objectives.title: Form a hypothesis
objectives.desc: Press B. Pin the proof and choose.
objectives.prompt: How did VELVET LOCUST cross the Bridges?

options.text: Tom Brooks did maintenance on the servers
options.feedback: Tom was in a meeting, file servers never initiate RDP, and there's no change ticket.

options.text: A worm exploited a vulnerability to spread automatically
options.feedback: Every hop used valid t.brooks credentials and admin tools. No exploit needed.

options.text: With stolen t.brooks credentials: SMB admin share + remote service to FS-CORE-01, then RDP through JUMP-02 to VAULT-DB-01

options.feedback: Follow the RDP source addresses. They went further.

objectives.success: Confirmed: lateral movement over SMB and RDP with valid credentials.
hints: Pin the ADMIN$ write and the RDP sessions.
Were the hops made with exploits or with credentials?
Pin e601 and e603, then choose the SMB + RDP option.

objectives.title: Map it to ATT&CK
objectives.desc: Press M and map all three findings.
hints: Two findings are about moving between systems; one is about running code on the target.
Lateral Movement: SMB/Windows Admin Shares and RDP. Execution: System Services.

objectives.title: Contain, all at once
objectives.desc: Press R. Coordinated containment: preserve, then cut every foothold at the same moment.
hints: Containing one host at a time lets them hop to another.
Capture triage first, then isolate the set together and remove the service.
Triage, disable t.brooks, coordinated isolation, remove the services.

f1.text: svchelper.exe copied to FS-CORE-01 and BACKUP-01 through the ADMIN$ share
f1.hint: They used a Windows file share to move.

f2.text: RDP sessions as t.brooks: FS-CORE-01 -> JUMP-02 -> VAULT-DB-01

f3.text: A remotely created service ran svchelper.exe as LocalSystem
f3.hint: The service control manager executed their binary.

responses.label: Capture triage (memory + disk) from FS-CORE-01, JUMP-02, BACKUP-01
responses.description: Run the EDR triage collector on all three.
responses.feedback: Triage captured. svchelper's config is in memory: it has a DNS fallback channel.

responses.label: Disable t.brooks and purge his Kerberos tickets everywhere
responses.description: Lock the account until IT re-issues it with MFA.
responses.tradeoff: Tom uses a temporary account for a day.
responses.feedback: t.brooks disabled. Every session using it drops.

responses.label: Coordinated isolation: WS-FIN-0142, FS-CORE-01, JUMP-02 at the same moment
responses.description: EDR network containment on all three in one change.
responses.tradeoff: Short outage of the file server; announced as maintenance.
responses.too_early: Preserve triage and kill the credentials first, or they'll simply log in somewhere else.
responses.feedback: All three footholds cut at once. No time for them to hop.

responses.label: Stop and delete the svchelper service on FS-CORE-01 and BACKUP-01
responses.description: Remove the service and quarantine svchelper.exe.
responses.too_early: Capture triage first. svchelper's config is only in memory.

responses.label: Enforce the admin paths: RDP to servers only from JUMP-02 with MFA
responses.description: Firewall rules plus finishing the MFA rollout for tier-0.
responses.tradeoff: Some admin friction. Closes the bridge permanently.
responses.feedback: File servers can no longer start RDP. MFA required for tier-0.

responses.label: Isolate FS-CORE-01 by itself right now
responses.description: Contain only the file server immediately.
responses.tradeoff: They still hold JUMP-02 and the vault session.
responses.feedback: They watched FS-CORE-01 drop and dug in on JUMP-02 and the vault. Contain the whole set together.

responses.label: Power off every server in the data center
responses.tradeoff: Destroys memory evidence and stops the business.
responses.feedback: Payroll, email, and the file shares are down, and the memory evidence is gone. Targeted containment beats a blackout.
